beats.why: The on-screen words only state 'deadly to your portfolio' without naming brand attachment or personal opinion, so the viewer inferred violating supply and demand rules.
The portfolio manager's smirking face led the viewer to believe the manager was dismissing the retail trader's plan rather than the retail trader playing devil's advocate against the strategy.
The on-screen words 'DEAFENING NOISE' in an abstract setting led the viewer to infer metaphorical market noise rather than physical factory floor machinery.
The trader holding a wallet with a smirk led the viewer to believe the narrator was advocating locking in financial gains rather than warning against the ego's trap of seeking bargains.
The words 'TOO LATE BY THEN' lacked the context of magazine covers and public euphoria, leading the viewer to guess it referred to public filings of institutional selling.
The words 'FINISHED THEIR ACCUMULATION' led the viewer to expect an upward markup rather than institutions preparing to sell to latecomers.
The labelled buckets diagram framed the statistical 75% trend correlation as a trader's decision between following or bucking the trend.
The storm cloud icon led the viewer to believe the narrator was warning of catastrophic losses rather than describing the conventional dogma to weather the storm.
The trader's smirk led the viewer to believe the narrator was criticizing amateur pattern labeling rather than chuckling at the odd names of chart patterns.
